title: The tetrahedral partition maximizes Gaussian noise stability for small positive correlations
summary: Proves dimension-independent Gaussian optimality and equality rigidity of the balanced tetrahedral partition for a qualitative interval of small positive correlations, using the imported equal-cell first-moment theorem and covariance deficit identity.
verification: Written analytic proof with explicit external inputs; warning-free LaTeX build, all-page visual inspection, isolated internal AI PDF-only reading and isolated source-archive build. No external specialist review or formal verification.
next_steps: Obtain specialist review of the imported covariance identity, quantitative alignment, weighted exterior estimate and normal-flux limit.
Audit novelty and the precise relation to earlier three-cell small-correlation arguments before selecting a submission venue.
abstract:
We prove that the regular tetrahedral partition maximizes Gaussian noise
stability among all measurable four-cell partitions of equal Gaussian
measure, for every sufficiently small positive correlation. The correlation
interval is independent of the ambient dimension, and equality determines
the tetrahedral partition up to orthogonal maps, labels and cylindrical
extension. We use Zhang's equal-cell first-moment theorem and balanced
covariance deficit identity to obtain quantitative moment alignment and a
first-moment interface form whose only zero modes are rotations. The
nonlinear argument normalizes transfers by their exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck
score regret. A weighted exterior estimate prevents the normalized
transfers from escaping to infinity, and their limiting normal flux
satisfies a sharp quadratic regret bound. The interaction converges to its
first-moment part, giving a rotational-kernel contradiction. The threshold
is qualitative; no conclusion for all positive correlations is asserted.
